Reference / cbor

cbor#

CBOR (RFC 8949) values: one immutable Cbor, decoded or built in code, read without casts and encoded by the runtime in one call.

Version: v1.0.0

Description#

CBOR (RFC 8949) values: one immutable Cbor, decoded or built in code, read without casts and encoded by the runtime in one call.

import "io/stdout" take Stdout;
let reply = Cbor(CborEntry("id", 4711), CborEntry("tags", Cbor(items: [Cbor("new"), Cbor(7)])));
let bytes = reply.encoding();
let read = ParsedCbor(bytes).root();
Stdout().writeln(bytes.size().string(), " bytes: ", read.string());
Stdout().writeln(read.get("id").int().string());
18 bytes: {"id": 4711, "tags": ["new", 7]}
4711

The data model maps onto Okkama values exactly:

  • integers of any size: major types 0 and 1, and bignums (tags 2 and 3) beyond 64 bits;
  • floats in the shortest width that keeps the value (half, single, double); a decoded infinity or NaN is kept, but is not an Okkama float;
  • rat as tag 30 (rational number, IANA registry): [numerator, denominator], reduced, the denominator positive;
  • text strings as string, byte strings as @byte (raw, no base64);
  • arrays, and maps with keys of any CBOR type (string and int keys have their own lookups; any key is a Cbor);
  • true and false as bool; null and undefined are absence, read through maybe();
  • tags other than 2, 3 and 30 are kept with their content (tag(), content()), and so are simple values (simple()).

Decoding refuses what is not well-formed, text that is not UTF-8, a map key repeated in its map, and bignum or rational tags with the wrong content, each as a CborError with the byte offset. It accepts indefinite lengths and is bounded: 128 levels deep, 1048576 data items and 16 MiB unless told otherwise. Encoding writes definite lengths only: encoding() keeps the map order as built or decoded (RFC 8949 4.1, preferred serialization), and canonical_encoding() sorts map keys by their encoded bytes (4.2.1, core deterministic encoding), the form to hash or sign.

Public API#

enum CborKind#

enum CborKind = (int_value, float_value, rat_value, text_value, bytes_value, boolean_value, null_value, undefined_value, simple_value, array_value, map_value, tagged_value)

Which kind of CBOR value a Cbor is.

  • int_value: An integer of any size.
  • float_value: A float, perhaps not finite.
  • rat_value: A rational number (tag 30).
  • text_value: A text string.
  • bytes_value: A byte string.
  • boolean_value: true or false.
  • null_value: null.
  • undefined_value: undefined.
  • simple_value: Another simple value: 0..19 or 32..255.
  • array_value: An array.
  • map_value: A map.
  • tagged_value: A tag other than 2, 3 and 30, with its content.

object Cbor#

object Cbor

One CBOR value, decoded or built: read it without casts, encode it in one call. Two Cbor values are the same data model value when their canonical_encoding() is equal.

let point = Cbor(CborEntry(1, Cbor(2.5)), CborEntry(2, Cbor(-1)));
let x = point.get(1).float();
let canonical = point.canonical_encoding();

Cbor.Cbor#

Cbor(tag is int, content is Cbor)

Tag number tag (0..2^64-1) over content, read as a decode reads it: tag 2 or 3 over bytes is an integer, tag 30 over [int, positive int] a rat, and any other content of those tags is CborError.refused_tag; other tags are kept: Cbor(tag: 32, content: Cbor("https://okkama.org")).

object CborEntry#

object CborEntry

One entry of a map: a key and its value. Text keys take scalars directly: CborEntry("id", 42), CborEntry("name", "Ada"), CborEntry("blob", bytes).

let header = Cbor(CborEntry(1, Cbor(-7)), CborEntry(Cbor(items: []), Cbor()));

object ParsedCbor#

object ParsedCbor

CBOR bytes decoded on the first root(): exactly one item, within the limits (128 levels of containers and tags, 1048576 data items, 16 MiB by default).

let bytes is @byte = [byte(0xa1), byte(0x61), byte(0x6e), byte(0x01)];
let n = ParsedCbor(bytes).root().get("n").int();
let small = ParsedCbor(origin: bytes, maximum_depth: 4, maximum_items: 16, maximum_size: 64);

ParsedCbor.ParsedCbor#

CBOR bytes and the limits of their decode, each positive.

ParsedCbor.root#

root() is Cbor

The decoded value, or the CborError of the first fault with its byte offset (CborError.trailing when bytes follow the item).

object CborItems#

object CborItems

The items of a CBOR sequence (RFC 8742) as a stream gives them, one at a time: each within the limits of ParsedCbor, the bytes held only until their item is read. A fault is a CborError at its offset in the stream; a stream that ends inside an item is CborError.truncated.

for await CborItems(origin: socket) -> item {
    item.get("op").text();
}

CborItems.CborItems#

CborItems(origin is AsyncReading, maximum_depth is int = 128, maximum_items is int = 1048576, maximum_size is int = 16777216)

Items of a stream within these limits, each positive.

object CborMaybeReader#

object CborMaybeReader

A value that may be absent: null, undefined or a missing key read as none. A value of another kind is still CborError.wrong_kind.

let doc = Cbor(CborEntry("note", Cbor()));
let note = doc.maybe("note").text() else "";

Errors#

enum CborError#

enum CborError is Error = (truncated(offset is int), malformed(offset is int, reason is string), invalid_utf8(offset is int), duplicate_key(offset is int), invalid_tag(offset is int, tag is int, reason is string), trailing(offset is int), too_deep(offset is int, limit is int), too_many_items(offset is int, limit is int), too_large(offset is int, limit is int), invalid_limit(name is string, amount is int), wrong_kind(expected is CborKind, actual is CborKind), missing_key(key is string), missing_index(index is int, size is int), unrepresentable(value is string), repeated_key(key is string), refused_tag(tag is int, reason is string))

Everything that goes wrong with CBOR. Decoding names the byte offset of the item at fault (the item that runs past the end, the malformed head, the repeated key, the first trailing byte, the item past a limit).

  • truncated: The input ends inside the item at offset.
  • malformed: Not well-formed CBOR (RFC 8949 Appendix F), and why.
  • invalid_utf8: A text string, or a chunk of one, that is not UTF-8.
  • duplicate_key: A map key equal to an earlier key of its map.
  • invalid_tag: A bignum (2, 3) or rational (30) tag with the wrong content.
  • trailing: Bytes after the item.
  • too_deep: Containers and tags nest deeper than limit.
  • too_many_items: More data items than limit.
  • too_large: More bytes than limit.
  • invalid_limit: A decode limit that is not positive.
  • wrong_kind: A read of another kind than the value's.
  • missing_key: A map has no such key, in diagnostic notation.
  • missing_index: An array index outside 0..size.
  • unrepresentable: A float that is not finite, read as an Okkama float.
  • repeated_key: Building a map gave the same key twice.
  • refused_tag: Building a tag of a number outside 0..2^64-1, or a bignum or rational tag over the wrong content.
